2. Heard the learned Counsel for the parties.
NC: 2024:KHC-K:5017 3.

Appellants herein and two others were charge sheeted for the offences punishable under Sections 498A & 323 IPC read with Sections 3 & 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961, in Crime No.85/2009 registered by Women Police Station, Gulbarga.

The appellants were arrayed as accused nos.1 to 5 in Hazratah Ali And Ors vs The State on 11 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104155731/

sentences.text: 4. The Trial Court had framed charges against all the seven accused who were charge sheeted and had read over the same to them.
Since the accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried, the prosecution in order to prove its charges against the accused, had examined 13 witnesses as PWs-1 to 13.
Seven documents were produced and marked as Exs.P-1 to P- 7.
After completion of the prosecution evidence, the Trial Court had recorded the statement of the accused under Section 313 of Cr.PC.

On behalf of the defence, one witness was examined as DW-1 and five documents were produced and marked as Exs.D-1 to D-5.
5.

After hearing the arguments addressed on both sides, the Trial Court vide its judgment and order dated 27.11.2014 passed in C.C.No.664/2010 acquitted all the accused of the NC: 2024:KHC-K:5017 charge sheeted offences.

The State had challenged the said judgment and order of acquittal before the Court of I Addl. District & Sessions Judge, Kalaburagi, in Crl.A.No.18/2015, which was partly allowed vide impugned judgment and order dated 06.11.2019.

entities.text: Court of I Addl. District & Sessions Judge, Kalaburagi

sentences.text: The Appellate Court vide the impugned judgment and order convicted accused nos.1 to 5 for the offences punishable under Section 498A & 323 IPC.

For the offence under Section 498A IPC, accused nos.1 to 5 were sentenced to undergo imprisonment for a period of three years and pay fine of Rs.5,000/- each and in default to undergo simple imprisonment for a period of two months.

For the offence under Section 323 IPC,
accused nos.1 to 5 were sentenced to pay fine of Rs.1,000/- each and in default to undergo simple imprisonment for a period of one month.
Accused 1 to 5 were acquitted for the offence punishable under Sections 3 & 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.

So far as accused nos.6 & 7 are concerned,
the judgment and order of acquittal passed by the Trial Court was confirmed against them.
Being aggrieved by the impugned judgment and order of conviction and sentence, accused nos.1 to 5 are before this Court.

Learned Counsel for the appellants having reiterated the grounds urged in the appeal memorandum, submits that the Appellate Court was not justified in convicting the appellants for the offences under Sections 498A & 323 IPC.
He submits that the material witnesses were not examined by the prosecution before the Trial Court and except PW-1, all the other witnesses are hearsay witnesses in the present case.
7. Per contra, learned HCGP has argued in support of the impugned judgment and order of conviction and has prayed to dismiss the appeal.
8. The prosecution in order to prove its charges against the accused, had examined 13 witnesses as PWs-1 to 13.
PW-1 is the first informant who is the wife of accused no.1.
PW-2 is the panch witness to the spot and seizure mahazar.
PW-3 is the friend of first informant's father.
PW-4 is the father of first informant.
PW-5 is the brother-in-law of first informant and PW-6 is the uncle of the first informant.
PWs-7 & 11 are the relatives of the first informant.

PWs-8, 9, 12 & 13 are the police officers and PW-10 is the Junior Engineer who had prepared the sketch of the alleged place of Hazratah Ali And Ors vs The State on 11 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104155731/
3 incident.

is the FIR and NC: 2024:KHC-K:5017 Ex.P-2 is the wedding card.
Ex . P-3

& P-5 are the spot mahazar and seizure mahazar, respectively.

9. The marriage of accused no.1 with PW-1 was solemnized on 25.05.2009 at Kalaburagi.

The allegation against the accused is that, after marriage, in the matrimonial home of PW-1 at Mumbai,
she was harassed and tortured in furtherance of the demand made by the accused persons for payment of additional dowry.
It is alleged that at the time of marriage, accused persons were given dowry.
PW-1 had stayed in her matrimonial house only for a period of about two months.

Since she was being abused and assaulted in her matrimonial house, she had returned to Kalaburagi along with her mother on 28.07.2009 and on 03.08.2009, accused nos.1 to 7 allegedly came to her parents house at Kalaburagi and assaulted her.
In respect of the said incident that had taken place on 03.08.2009, first information was lodged by PW-1 on 28.09.2009.
PW-1 has stated that all the accused persons used to abuse and assault her in her matrimonial house in furtherance of their demand for payment of dowry.
She has deposed that unable to bear the ill-treatment meted out on her by the accused, she had called her mother to Mumbai, and thereafter returned to Kalaburagi on 28.07.2009.
Except PW-1, there is no other witness examined by the prosecution to prove the allegations about cruelty being committed by the accused persons on her at Mumbai.
According to PW-1, her mother had come to Mumbai and had brought her back since she was being abused and assaulted in her matrimonial house.
The mother of PW-1 has not been examined in the present case by the prosecution.
11. PW-2 is the panch witness to the spot mahazar - Ex.P-4 and seizure mahazar - Ex.P-5.
His evidence would not be helpful to the prosecution to prove the charges against the accused persons.
12. PW-3 is the friend of PW-4.

According to the prosecution, PW-3 was present in the house of PW-1's parents on 03.08.2009 when allegedly accused nos.1 to 7 had assaulted NC:
2024:KHC-K:5017 PW-1 in her parents house.
But, PW-3 during the course of his cross-examination has stated that he was not present at the spot on 03.08.2009.
13. PW-4 is the father of PW-1.
This witness is a hearsay witness in so far as the allegation of cruelty against the accused persons, which allegedly was committed by them in Mumbai.

This witness has stated that his daughter had informed him over phone about the harassment by the accused persons, and therefore, his wife and son-in-law had gone to Mumbai and they had brought PW-1 back along with them to Kalaburagi.
It is not the case of PW-1 that along with her mother, her brother-in-law also had come to Mumbai and she had returned to Kalaburagi along with them.
The son-in-law of PW-4 viz., Fayazuddin who had accompanied the mother of PW-1 to Mumbai is also not examined in the present case.

sentences.text: PWs-5 to 7 & 11 who are the relatives of PW-1 are also hearsay witnesses with regard to the allegation of cruelty committed by the accused on PW-1 at Mumbai.

According to the prosecution,
PW-1 had returned to Kalaburagi on 28.07.2009 along with her mother, and thereafter, she was NC:
2024:KHC-K:5017 staying in her parents house.
On 03.08.2009, accused nos.1 to 7 allegedly came to the house of PW-1 at Kalaburagi and had abused and assaulted her.
In respect of the alleged incident that had taken place on 03.08.2009, first information is lodged belatedly on 28.09.2009.
No proper explanation is given by the prosecution for the inordinate delay in lodging the FIR.
According to PW-1, after the alleged incident that had taken place on 03.08.2009, she fell unconscious and thereafter she was shifted to the hospital.
But, there are no medical records produced by the prosecution nor the doctor who had treated PW-1 is examined by the prosecution in the present case.
A perusal of the charge sheet would go to show that the prosecution has not even recorded the statement of the Medical Officer and has not even cited him as charge sheet witness in the present case.
In the first information, it is stated that after the alleged incident that had taken place on 03.08.2009, there was a panchayath held, and thereafter, the first information was lodged.

The prosecution has failed to examine any witnesses to prove that such a panchayath was held after the alleged incident of 03.08.2009.
- 10 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:5017 15.
As observed earlier, except PW-1, the prosecution has not examined any other witness to prove the allegation of cruelty committed by the accused on PW-1 in Mumbai.

All the other independent witnesses who are examined in the present case are examined to prove the alleged incident that had taken place on 03.08.2009 in the parents house of PW-1.
16.
Accused no.7 is the brother-in-law of accused no.1 and accused no.6 is his wife.

Accused nos.6 &
7 are the residents of Raichur.
Accused no.7 was employed in Hatti Gold Mines in Raichur.
DW-1 - Kariyappa is the Deputy Manager of Hatti Gold Mines.
This witness was examined by the defence to prove that on 03.08.2009, accused no.7 had attended work in Hatti Gold Mines.
His attendance register is marked as Ex.D-3.
The attendance certificate is marked as Ex.D-2.
Ex.D-4 is another attendance register to show that even on 25.09.2009, accused no.7 was on duty.
Ex.D-5 is the work assignment register.

By examining PW-1 and producing Exs.D-1 to D-5, the defence has proved that accused no.7 was not present on 03.08.2009 in the house of PW-1's parents, and therefore, a serious doubt arises with regard to the alleged incident that had taken place on 03.08.2009.

The prosecution has failed to produce any material to show that accused nos.1 to 5 had traveled from Mumbai to Kalaburagi and had participated in the alleged incident that had taken place in the house of PW-1's parents on 03.08.2009.

In view of the inordinate delay of 55 days in approaching the police in respect of the alleged incident that had taken place on 03.08.2009 and also having Hazratah Ali And Ors vs The State on 11 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104155731/

sentences.text:
regard to the fact that the prosecution has failed to produce any material before the court to prove that PW-1 who allegedly fell unconscious after the incident on 03.08.2009 and she was taken to the hospital for treatment, a serious doubt arises with regard to the alleged incident that had taken place in the house of PW-1's parents house on 03.08.2009.
18.

According to PW-1, after the marriage, her mother had come for the first time to Mumbai after she had informed her parents about the ill-treatment meted out on her by the accused and she had returned with her mother to Kalaburagi.
Ex. P-3
is the photograph taken in the matrimonial house of PW-1.
In the said photograph, along with PW-1, her husband (accused no.1), mother and brother are also found.

Therefore,
- 12 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:5017 the correctness of the statement of PW-1 that her mother had come for the first time to Mumbai only to bring her back to Kalaburagi also becomes doubtful.
19. The Trial Court having appreciated all these aspects of the matter had rightly acquitted the accused of the charge sheeted offences.

The Appellate Court, however, without properly appreciating the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the prosecution, has erred in convicting accused nos.1 to 5 for the offences under Sections 498A & 323 IPC, more so, when it has acquitted the said accused for the offences under Sections 3 & 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.

20. It is trite that in an appeal against acquittal, unless it is found that the judgment and order of acquittal is prima facie illegal and perverse, the Appellate Court should not interfere with the judgment and order of acquittal.

Under the circumstances, I am of the opinion that the Appellate Court was not justified in setting aside the judgment and order of acquittal passed by the Trial Court and convicting accused - 13 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:5017 nos.1 to 5 for the offences under Sections 498A & 323 IPC.

Accordingly, the following order:
21.
The appeal is allowed.

The judgment and order of conviction and sentence dated 06.11.2019 passed by the Court of I Addl. District & Sessions Judge, Kalaburagi, in Crl.A.No.18/2015 convicting accused nos.1 to 5 for the offences under Sections 498A & 323 IPC, is set aside.
